title: Ex-Infosys Executives’ CortexSpark Ventures Launches ₹1,000 Cr Deeptech Fund
summary: Ex-Infosys executives launch CortexSpark Ventures with a Rs 1,000 crore deeptech fund
detailed: Former Infosys executives Vinay Peshwa and Sanjay Khanduri launched CortexSpark Ventures and its debut Viksit Bharat Fund-I with a ₹1,000 Cr target corpus and a ₹400 Cr greenshoe option.
The Category II AIF aims to back roughly 20 startups across six deeptech sectors with average cheque sizes between $4 million and $5 million.
The fund targets proprietary tech in spacetech, defence, embodied AI, enterprise AI, medtech, and energy, backed by SEBI registration.
This matters as institutional capital targets India's deeptech ecosystem, which saw startup funding rise 176% YoY in Q3 2026.
sentences: The fund has an additional ₹400 Cr greenshoe option, taking its potential size to ₹1,400 Cr (about $150 Mn).
It has secured SEBI registration as a Category II AIF under the name CortexSpark Ventures Alpha Fund, the firm said.
The fund plans to back around 20 startups, with an average cheque size of $4 Mn to $5 Mn.

The fund will back startups working on proprietary technologies across six sectors – spacetech, defence tech, embodied AI and robotics, enterprise AI, medtech and bio-AI, and energy and advanced materials.
“India has built world-class technology services companies.
The next opportunity is to create globally competitive technology product companies driven by original research and intellectual property,” Peshwa said.
Peshwa is an IIT Kanpur alumnus with nearly three decades of experience in software, banking technology and startup investing.
He was involved in developing Infosys Finacle and has made more than 30 angel investments, mainly in AI and deeptech startups.
Khanduri holds degrees from IIT (BHU) and IIM Lucknow, as well as an MBA from Wharton.
He previously worked with Citigroup, Infosys, and Standard Chartered Bank in global capital markets and alternative investments.
CortexSpark Ventures will focus on startups with proprietary technology, strong technical foundations, experienced founders, and clear commercialisation plans.
It plans to assess potential investments through scientific evaluation and commercial due diligence, particularly in sectors that involve longer development cycles and higher capital requirements.
The firm is also developing CortexSpark OS, an AI-based platform to support deal sourcing, screening, due diligence, and portfolio monitoring.
Beyond funding, it will help portfolio startups with product development, hiring and business growth, while connecting them with enterprise customers, international markets and follow-on investors.
The fund’s investment committee will be chaired by Manoj Kohli, former country head of SoftBank Group and former CEO and MD of Bharti Airtel.

Its advisory committee will include two Padma Shri-awardee scientists – N Vedachalam, former director of ISRO’s Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre, and Ashutosh Sharma, former secretary of the Department of Science and Technology and Institute Chair Professor at IIT Kanpur.
The fund launch comes amid rising investor interest in India’s deeptech ecosystem.
Last week, Oister Global launched a ₹600 Cr growth-stage deeptech fund.
Meanwhile, Unacademy cofounders Gaurav Munjal and Roman Saini are also reportedly raising a ₹700 Cr fund, Longshot Capital, to invest in AI and deeptech startups.
According to Inc42’s ‘Indian Tech Startup Funding Report, Q3 2026’, deeptech startups raised $290 Mn across 28 deals during the quarter, up 176% from $105 Mn across 29 deals a year earlier.
This compared with a 5% increase in overall startup funding to $2.2 Bn.
